Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for the quick sync today. Short recap and proposed next steps below so we’re aligned.

Call recap (high level):
- Primary use: real-time customer-facing assistant + analytics pipelines.
- Expected steady-state volume: ~50M tokens/month (model input+output).
- Peak patterns: short bursts during business hours, estimated 200 concurrent sessions peak.
- Latency SLO: p95 interactive latency target = ~250ms for short responses (<= 64 tokens).
- Budget: you mentioned a working range of $10k–$20k/month and wanting to understand unit economics (target $/1M tokens).

Pricing/qualification asks from us:
1) Confirm monthly token volume range (low, expected, high).
2) Clarify hard latency SLO vs acceptable percentile trade-offs (p50/p95/p99).
3) Any compliance/regulatory constraints impacting deployment mode (hosted vs private)?

Preliminary unit economics (ballpark):
- Hosted API (standard): ~$15 / 1M tokens — balanced latency and cost for most production workloads.
- Hosted streaming + low-latency tier: premium ~ +20–40% depending on model (gives fastest first-token times).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): effective units can reach ~$7–$10 / 1M tokens depending on commit and utilization.

Latency vs cost trade-offs we discussed:
- Streaming reduces perceived time-to-first-token but has modest CPU overhead; if you care about p50 first-byte it’s great.
- Batching improves cost per token substantially but increases tail latency — good for async workloads or SLOs that allow slightly higher p95.
- Autoscaling + burst capacity lets you keep low steady costs and handle peaks but requires a short warm-up for large model kernels unless you use pre-warmed pools.

Next steps I propose:
1) Samir/Elena: confirm month token low/expected/high and target monthly budget range.
2) Redwood: we’ll produce a 2-week PoC plan (dedicated trial vs hosted eval) + detailed cost worksheet showing $/1M token sensitivity by batch size and SLO.
3) Schedule 30-min follow-up early next week to review the PoC scope and pricing options.

Attaching a pricing snapshot (Q1) and will have Aditya add a short technical note on batching vs streaming impacts.

Hi Samir — quick technical note to complement Marissa’s pricing notes.

Streaming vs batching (short):
- Streaming: best for perceived latency — you get first-token immediately and can show partial responses. Overhead: higher per-request CPU and more RPCs; this can increase cost slightly for tiny responses. Great when p50/p95 first-byte matters.
- Batching: combines many inferences into one kernel run, improving GPU utilization and lowering $/token. Trade-off: more tail latency (p95/p99) because requests wait in a batch window. If your SLO targets p95 <= 300ms, batching windows must be tiny (10–30ms) which reduces batching efficiency.
- Hybrid: start streaming the first bytes to meet perceived-latency SLO, then switch to batched processing for long-running completions where possible. Implementation depends on model architecture and SDK support; we have patterns to do this for chat-like flows.

Quantization / model choice: smaller quantized models reduce cost and latency. Dedicated pools let you pick the sweet spot: run a quantized 8-bit for common prompts and fall back to larger models for long-form tasks.

Sample unit economics (very rough):
- Hosted standard: $15 / 1M tokens -> 50M tokens = $750 / month. (note: this is illustrative; final price may include per-request overheads and streaming premiums)
- Hosted low-latency tier (streaming optimized): $18–$21 / 1M tokens -> 50M = ~$900–$1,050
- Dedicated reserved (6–12mo commit): ~$7–$10 / 1M tokens at high utilization -> 50M = $350–$500
Examples for your scenarios:
- Expected (35–50M): Hosted standard = ~$525–$750 / mo; Dedicated (commit) = ~$245–$500 / mo (depending on commit and utilization).
- High (120M): Hosted = ~$1,800; Dedicated = ~$840–$1,200.

Important: these numbers assume stable utilization and do not include extra costs like egress, enterprise support, or premium SLOs. Adapting batch sizes aggressively can cut hosted token unit cost by 20–40% but only if your latency SLO allows it.

If helpful, I can produce a 3-scenario spreadsheet (low/expected/high) showing sensitivity to batch window (5/20/50ms) and streaming fraction.
